text:
$\mathrm{SO}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$ on reaction with excess of water results into acidic mixture

$\mathrm{SO}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}\to \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}+2\mathrm{HCl}$

16 moles of $\mathrm{NaOH}$ is required for the complete neutralisation of the resultant acidic mixture. The number of moles of $\mathrm{SO}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$ used is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{SO}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}\to \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}+2\mathrm{HCl}$

Moles of $\mathrm{NaOH}$ required for complete neutralization of resultant acidic mixture $=16$ moles

And 1 mole of $\mathrm{SO}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$ produced 4 moles of $\mathrm{H}^{+}$.

$\therefore$ Moles of $\mathrm{SO}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$ used will be $=\frac{16}{4}=4$ moles
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift

text: The depression in freezing point observed for a formic acid solution of concentration $0.5\mathrm{mL}\mathrm{L}^{-1}$ is $0.0405^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$. Density of formic acid is $1.05\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mL}^{-1}$. The Van't Hoff factor of the formic acid solution is nearly : (Given for water $\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}=1.86\mathrm{k}\mathrm{kg}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{f}}$ of formic acid $=0.0405^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$

Concentration $=0.5\mathrm{mL}/\mathrm{L}$

and density $=1.05\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{mL}$

$\therefore$ Mass of formic acid in solution $=1.05\times 0.5\mathrm{g}$

$=0.525\mathrm{g}$

$\therefore$ According to Van't Hoff equation,

$\begin{array}{l} \Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{f}}=\mathrm{i}\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}\cdot \mathrm{m} \\ 0.0405=\mathrm{i}\times 1.86\times \dfrac{0.525}{46\times 1} \end{array}$

(Assuming mass of $1\mathrm{L}$ water $=1\mathrm{kg}$ )

$\mathrm{i}=\frac{0.0405\times 46}{1.86\times 0.525}=1.89\approx 1.9$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift

text:
$20\mathrm{mL}$ of $0.1\mathrm{M}\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$ is mixed with $40\mathrm{mL}$ of $0.05\mathrm{M}\mathrm{HCl}$. The $\mathrm{pH}$ of the mixture is nearest to :

(Given : $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH})=1\times 10^{-5},\log 2=0.30,\log 3=0.48,\log 5=0.69,\log 7=0.84,\log 11=1.04)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$: $20\times 0.1=2$ mmol; $\mathrm{HCl}$: $40\times 0.05=2$ mmol, so the two neutralise each other completely:


[IMG]

$[\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}{}^{+}]=\dfrac{2\text{mmol}}{60\text{mL}}=\dfrac{1}{30}\text{M}$

$\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}$ is a salt of a weak base and a strong acid, so its solution is acidic by hydrolysis of $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}{}^{+}$:

$\mathrm{pH}=7-\dfrac{1}{2}(\mathrm{p}K_{b}+\log C)=7-\dfrac{1}{2}\left (5+\log \dfrac{1}{30}\right )$

With $\log 30=\log 3+1=1.48$:

$\mathrm{pH}=7-\dfrac{1}{2}(5-1.48)=7-1.76=5.24\approx 5.2$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift

text:
Among the following species

$\mathrm{N}_{2},\mathrm{N}_{2}^{+},\mathrm{N}_{2}^{-},\mathrm{N}_{2}^{2-},\mathrm{O}_{2},\mathrm{O}_{2}^{+},\mathrm{O}_{2}^{-},\mathrm{O}_{2}^{2-}$

the number of species showing diamagnetism is $_______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A species is diamagnetic only when all its electrons are paired. Up to 14 electrons the molecular orbitals fill as $σ1s,σ^{\ast }1s,σ2s,σ^{\ast }2s,(π2p_{x}=π2p_{y}),σ2p_{z}$; further electrons enter the degenerate pair $π^{\ast }2p_{x}=π^{\ast }2p_{y}$.

$\mathrm{N}{}_{2}$ (14 electrons): $\ldots (π2p)^{4}(σ2p_{z})^{2}$, all paired, diamagnetic.

$\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{+}$ (13 electrons): $\ldots (π2p)^{4}(σ2p_{z})^{1}$, 1 unpaired electron.

$\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{-}$ and $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{+}$ (15 electrons each): $(π^{\ast }2p_{x})^{1}$, 1 unpaired electron.

$\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{2-}$ and $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ (16 electrons each): $(π^{\ast }2p_{x})^{1}(π^{\ast }2p_{y})^{1}$, 2 unpaired electrons.

$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{-}$ (17 electrons): $(π^{\ast }2p_{x})^{2}(π^{\ast }2p_{y})^{1}$, 1 unpaired electron.

$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{2-}$ (18 electrons): $(π^{\ast }2p_{x})^{2}(π^{\ast }2p_{y})^{2}$, all paired, diamagnetic.

Only $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{2-}$ are diamagnetic.

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift

text: The enthalpy of combustion of propane, graphite and dihydrogen at $298\mathrm{K}$ are $-2220.0\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1},-393.5\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ and $-285.8\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ respectively. The magnitude of enthalpy of formation of propane $(\mathrm{C}_{3}\mathrm{H}_{8})$ is $_______________$ $\mathrm{kJ}\quad \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Enthalpy of combustion of propane, graphite and $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ at $298\mathrm{K}$ are

$\mathrm{C}_{3}\mathrm{H}_{8}(\mathrm{g})+5\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\to 3\mathrm{CO}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+4\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l}),\Delta \mathrm{H}_{1}=-2220\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

 $\mathrm{C}($ graphite $)+\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\to \mathrm{CO}_{2}(\mathrm{g}),\Delta \mathrm{H}_{2}=-393.5\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

$\mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\to \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l}),\Delta \mathrm{H}_{3}=-285.8\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

The desired reaction is

$3\mathrm{C}$ (graphite) + $4\mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\to \mathrm{C}_{3}\mathrm{H}_{8}(\mathrm{g})$

$\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{f}}=3\Delta \mathrm{H}_{2}+4\Delta \mathrm{H}_{3}-\Delta \mathrm{H}_{1}$

$\begin{array}{l} =3(-393.5)+4(-285.8)-(-2220) \\ =-103.7\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1} \end{array}$

$|\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{f}}|\simeq 104\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift

text:
The cell potential for $\mathrm{Zn}\left |\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})\right |\left |\mathrm{Sn}^{x+}\right |\mathrm{Sn}$ is $0.801\mathrm{V}$ at $298\mathrm{K}$. The reaction quotient for the above reaction is $10^{-2}$. The number of electrons involved in the given electrochemical cell reaction is $____________$.

$(~$ Given $:\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}|\mathrm{Zn}}^{\mathrm{o}}=-0.763\mathrm{V},\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Sn}^{x+}|\mathrm{Sn}}^{\mathrm{o}}=+0.008\mathrm{V}$ and $\left. \frac{2.303\mathrm{RT}}{\mathrm{F}}=0.06\mathrm{V}\right )$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{A}:\mathrm{Zn}\to \mathrm{Zn}^{2+}+2e^{-}$

$\mathrm{C}:\mathrm{Sn}^{+\mathrm{x}}+\mathrm{xe}^{-}\to \mathrm{Sn}$

$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Cell}}^{\circ }=\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Zn}|\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}}^{\circ }+\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Sn}^{+x}|\mathrm{Sn}}^{\circ }$

$\Rightarrow 0.763+0.008=0.771\mathrm{V}$

From the Nernst equation,

$\mathrm{E}_{\text{Cell}}=\mathrm{E}_{\text{Cell}}^{\circ }-\frac{2.303\mathrm{RT}}{\mathrm{nF}}\log \mathrm{Q}$

$0.801=0.771-\frac{0.06}{\mathrm{n}}\log 10^{-2}$

$0.03=\frac{0.06}{n}\times 2$

$\mathrm{n}=4$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift

text: The half life for the decomposition of gaseous compound $\mathrm{A}$ is $240\mathrm{s}$ when the gaseous pressure was 500 Torr initially. When the pressure was 250 Torr, the half life was found to be $4.0$ min. The order of the reaction is $______________. ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left (\mathrm{t}_{1/2}\right )_{\mathrm{A}}=240\mathrm{s}$ when $\mathrm{P}=500$ torr

$\left (t_{1/2}\right )_{A}=4\min =4\times 60=240$ sec when $P=250$ torr

It means half-life is independent of concentration of reactant present.

$\therefore$ Order of reaction $=1$

text:
Consider the following metal complexes :

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]^{3+}$

$[\mathrm{CoCl}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}]^{2+}$

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-}$

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})]^{3+}$

The spin-only magnetic moment value of the complex that absorbs light with shortest wavelength is $_____________ B. M. ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In all complexes, Co is present in $+3$ oxidation state and all complexes are low spin or inner orbital complex.

The stronger the ligand, the higher the crystal field splitting.

So, the order of crystal field splitting is

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-}>[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]^{3+}>[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})]^{3+}>$ $[\mathrm{CoCl}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}]^{2+}$

Shortest wavelength is shown by complex having maximum crystal field splitting.


[IMG]

Spin only magnetic moment $=\sqrt{0(0+2)}=0$ B.M

text: Among $Co^{3+}, Ti^{2+}, V^{2+}$ and $Cr^{2+}$ ions, one if used as a reagent cannot liberate $H_{2}$ from dilute mineral acid solution, its spin-only magnetic moment in gaseous state is $___________ B.M. ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ will not liberate $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ gas on reaction with dilute acid

$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Co}^{3+}/\mathrm{Co}^{2+}}^{\mathrm{O}}=+1.97$

And $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ has electronic configuration $=[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{6}$

$\therefore 4$ unpaired $\mathrm{e}^{-}$ are present in it

$\therefore$ Spin-only magnetic moment $=\sqrt{4(4+2)}=4.92\approx 5$

text: While estimating the nitrogen present in an organic compound by Kjeldahl's method, the ammonia evolved from $0.25\mathrm{g}$ of the compound neutralized $2.5\mathrm{mL}$ of $2~\mathrm{M}\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$. The percentage of nitrogen present in organic compound is $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ gas is neutralized by $2.5\mathrm{mL}$ of $2\mathrm{M}\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$

$\therefore$ Moles of $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ neutralized $=2.5\times 2\times 2$ millimole

$=10\times 10^{-3}\text{moles}$

$\therefore$ Weight of $\mathrm{N}$ present in the compound will be

$\begin{array}{l} =10\times 10^{-3}\times 14 \\ =0.14\mathrm{g} \end{array}$

$\therefore %$ of ' $\mathrm{N}$ ' in compound

$\begin{array}{l} =\dfrac{0.14}{0.25}\times 100 \\ =56% \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift
